title: ASEAN Summit Day 2: China's trade pitch, scams talk, Trump next
summary: China cast itself as ASEAN’s free-trade partner as leaders tackled online scams and prepared for Donald Trump’s arrival in Manila.

blocks.text: November 16, 2026 | 7:40pm

MANILA, Philippines — Chinese Premier Li Qiang pitched Beijing to Southeast Asian leaders on Monday, November 16, as a defender of free trade and multilateralism, a day before United States President Donald Trump swings by for the tail end of ASEAN summit in Manila.

"Although economic and trade restrictions have substantially increased around the world, we remain firmly committed to safeguarding multilateralism and promoting free trade and endeavor to make the pie of cooperation bigger," Li said.
Li spoke at one of four summits ASEAN leaders held with major partners on the second day of the bloc's 49th summit alongside meetings with the United Nations, Australia and South Korea.
Foreign Affairs Secretary Theresa Lazaro confirmed online scams and transnational crime were raised in all four "plus one" meetings.
Trade between China and ASEAN
Describing the past five years of China and ASEAN ties as "truly extraordinary," Li cited more than $1 trillion in China-ASEAN trade last year and over $500 billion in cumulative two-way investment.
Amid rising unilateralism and protectionism, he said, China and ASEAN must "stand united, ward off interference, and work together."

President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. in his opening remarks at the ASEAN-China summit had also made known to the bloc that ASEAN and China must "continue to find common ground and pursue tangible cooperation" even amid "regional and global uncertainties."
China is ASEAN's largest trading partner, but major Southeast Asian economies are also seeking closer ties with Washington amid trade uncertainty under Trump.

Trump arrives on Tuesday to meet ASEAN leaders and attend the first Quad leaders' meeting in two years with Japan, Australia and India, before flying to the APEC forum in Shenzhen, where a three-way meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin is scheduled.
Peaceful settlement of disputes

Marcos — who last month flagged Beijing's ambassador to Manila Jing Quan for remarks that sounded "like a threat" after the latter said China could "easily win" in the event of a conflict — also had choice remarks for ASEAN and China's need to respect international law.
Jing was seen sitting beside Li during the summit, across from Marcos and Lazaro.

"During this anniversary year, our shared commitment to international law and the peaceful settlement of disputes must be reflected in our actions, including through self-restraint, mutual respect, and practical cooperation," Marcos said.
Marcos also noted the ASEAN-China summit marked the 35th anniversary of dialogue relations and the fifth year of the two sides' comprehensive strategic partnership.
Lazaro said they adopted four documents, including statements on energy and forestry cooperation.
Dialogue partners
"This issue of scams, online scams, and transnational crime seems to be prevalent among the four dialogue partners," Lazaro told reporters on Monday evening.

At the ASEAN-UN summit, UN Secretary-General António Guterres warned that armed conflict, rising energy costs and growing humanitarian needs were straining the region, citing the war in Ukraine and Middle East crises that have disrupted key maritime routes.

Lazaro said leaders agreed to work with UN agencies against cybercrime and the misuse of artificial intelligence, and described the protection of migrant workers as one of the most important issues discussed.

On the summit's sidelines, Guterres called for the release of Myanmar's former state counsellor Aung San Suu Kyi and said aerial bombardment had become the leading cause of civilian casualties in the country.
He backed ASEAN leaders' decision on Sunday to pursue "calibrated engagement" with Myanmar, but said the violence must stop.
He also said the UN was ready to support any denuclearization effort arising from this week's meeting among the leaders of the US, China and Russia.
Marcos and Guterres also separately discussed UN reform and the selection of his successor, who takes office on Jan. 1, 2027.

At the sixth ASEAN-Australia summit, Prime Minister Anthony Albanese announced an ASEAN-Australia digital economy program to support AI safety and digital trade standards, and leaders discussed upgrading the ASEAN-Australia-New Zealand Free Trade Area.

South Korean President Lee Jae-myung, who arrived in Manila on Monday, proposed initiatives on artificial intelligence and creative industries at the ASEAN-South Korea summit and said talks to expand their free trade agreement were progressing.
